the_one_thing_if_you_read_nothing_else: THE ARTIFACT THIS ROUTE WILL POST IS IN JAPANESE AND EVERY SURVEYED VENUE READS ENGLISH. Four laps had this route elected, the venue rule quoted, the artifact checked against that rule and passing, an owner request filed on the strength of it — and no field on any venue row described the reader. It was found by opening assets/free-demo/index.html and reading line 2: lang="ja". The general form is NOT 'check the language'. It is that every field on those rows described the VENUE or described US, and none described the MEETING of the two. Postability was fully modelled; fit was not modelled at all. Before trusting any row that reads open, ask what it would take for the thing to WORK, not just to be permitted — a row can only answer questions somebody gave it a field for.

the_thing_worth_reading_twice: A MODEL ANSWERS ONLY THE QUESTIONS SOMEBODY GAVE IT A FIELD FOR. The venue rows were carefully built: rule_quoted, eligibility_threshold, live_slot_evidence, postable_when, account, postable_today — six sessions of work, each field added because its absence had cost something. Every one of them answers 'may we post' and none answers 'will it work'. So the row read one owner fact from open while the thing it would post was in a language its readers do not read, and the row was RIGHT: it was never asked. The previous two sessions found unread records — correct data with no reader. This is the next layer down and it is harder to see, because there is no unread field to point at. The question was never written. When a row reads open, do not only ask which script reads it; ask what it does not have a column for.

The first rebase conflicted in state/eta.json on the fetched_at line alone and was resolved by hand — take the incoming timestamp, then re-run compute-eta --local --write.
